subject.title: fix(security): narrow two audit false positives for single-operator multi-agent setups

question: Should allowlist-with-configured group targets stop counting as a multi-user signal for every channel scope, or only for narrower single-operator multi-account patterns?
rationale: The PR intentionally reduces a security-audit warning surface, and source/docs evidence shows root channel allowlists can still be shared-user ingress unless sender allowlists are configured.

options.title: Narrow only the false-positive scope
options.body: Preserve the root/shared-channel allowlist signal and suppress or downgrade only the single-operator multi-account cases that the linked issue reports.

options.title: Accept broad suppression
options.body: Allow all scoped allowlists with configured targets to stop triggering the heuristic, but update docs and require maintainer security sign-off for the reduced warning surface.

options.title: Pause for a broader audit design
options.body: Hold this PR until the older same-issue design that keeps scoped signals in detail when broadening exists is revived or replaced.

recommendation.title: Narrow only the false-positive scope
recommendation.body: Preserve the root/shared-channel allowlist signal and suppress or downgrade only the single-operator multi-account cases that the linked issue reports.
